Dr. Jayant Narlikar Padma Vibhushan Indian Astrophysicist delivered a talk on "Anomalous Redshifts - A Glimpse of the World beyond Earth" Dr. Anil Kakodkar Padma Vibhushan Indian Nuclear Physicist addressed VITians on "Taking India Forward - Role of Educational Institutes" Dr. Raghunath Mashelkar Padma Vibhushan Former Director General of CSIR addressed VITians on "Building India as a Science, Technology and Innovation Superpower" Dr. Man Mohan Sharma Padma Vibhushan Chemical Engineer, Scientist Teacher addressed VITians on "Life of a Teacher, Researcher Consultant in an University" Dr. Kirit Parikh Padma Bhushan Economist and Technologist addressed VITians on "Low Carbon Strategy for Inclusive Growth" Dr. Shashikumar Chitre Padma Bhushan Indian Mathematician and Astrophysicist addressed VITians on "Origin of Life in the Universe" Dr. Deepak Phatak Padma Shree Engineer Educationist gave mantra of "Learn, Earn and Return" to graduating VITians Dr. Ganapati Yadav Padma Shree Chemical Engineer, Inventor Academician delivered a talk on "Smart Materials in Chemistry" Dr. Sharad Kale Padma Shree Scientist Expert in Waste Reuse delivered a talk on "Environmental Sustainability" lIFE @VIT Life @VIT TESTIMONIALS Hear it from our Stakeholder Rushabh Sanghavi / Alumnus Vidyalankar Institute of Technology provides the best platform and infrastructure through digitally equipped campus; with a homely environment. Various e-learning resources like v-Live, Impartus Lecture Capture, online doubt solving sessions, along with numerous extra-curricular activities provide avenues for positive career development. I always feel connected with my alma mater because of VIT’s ‘Alumni Association’. Vaishali Paradkar / Parent VIT campus has excellent infrastructure, well-equipped labs, great library and the faculty members are well experienced, highly qualified and always willing to help the students. రోహిణి మల్లాది / విద్యార్థి VIT Online classes మరియు study material వల్ల, నేను ఎక్కడి నుంచి అయినా, ఎప్పుడు సమయం వీలు పడితే అప్పుడు చదువుకోవడానికి, నేర్చుకోవడానికి వీలు అవుతోంది. Rushil Dahisaria / Alumnus My engineering journey at VIT has been immensely encouraging because of generous, passionate, and enthusiastic faculty. Here, the course of the study is aimed at delivering practical solutions through innovative laboratory experiments that have imbibed a spirit of teamwork and dedication within me. Dr. Meenakshi Arya / Former Teacher It was my honour to be a part of VIT. A very positive teaching-learning environment, great pool of motivated faculty, very talented and enthusiastic students makes my tenure at VIT one of my most memorable one. My best wishes to VIT for its future endeavours. Prof. Vaishali Gurav / Parent Admission to Vidyalankar has been the best investment we made for both my sons. VIT groomed my sons technically and made them industry ready professionals. The laboratories, library, indoor and outdoor sports facilities and canteen services are outstanding at VIT. I am very grateful to VIT for providing such a wonderful teaching learning experience to its students. डॉ. संगीता भट / पालक व्ही आई टी हे एक उत्तम इंजीनियरिंग महाविद्यालय आसा.हे महाविद्यालय विद्यार्थ्यांचे सर्वांगीण अभिव्रधीचे उद्देश दवर्न कार्य कर्ता आसा. हे व्यक्त कर्चाक माका खूप आनंद जाता.ह्या संस्थेचे आवरण खूप विशाल असा आणि त्या आवरणात सुसज्जीत प्रयोगशाळा आणि सगळे अनुकूलता आसा. ह्या संस्थेचे शिक्षकगण सगळे विद्यार्थीले प्रगतीक प्रयत्नशील आसा. অনির্বান দত্ত / ছাত্র বিদ্যালঙ্কার আমার জন্য একটা আলাদা অভিগ্গতা। নিজের ঘর ছেড়ে মুম্বাই আসার পর, আমার একমাত্র সাহারা, যে আমাকে নতুন করে পরিচয় দিয়েছে একটা সম্পূর্ণ নতুন জায়গায়। এক অসাধারণ কেম্পাসের, সাক্ষী আমরা। পড়াশোনা এবং সাংস্কৃতিক চর্চার জন্য এক উন্নত মানের পরিবেশ। আমি এই প্রতিষ্ঠানের ছাত্র হতে পেরে গর্বিত। ସଞ୍ଜୟ କୁମାର ବଳ / ଅଭିଭାବକ ସର୍ଵାଧୁନିକ ଶିକ୍ଷାପ୍ରଦ ସୁବିଧା ସହ ଉଚ୍ଚ ଯୋଗ୍ୟତା ସମ୍ପନ୍ନ ଶିକ୍ଷାବିତ୍ ଓ ସମସ୍ତ ପ୍ରକାର ଅତ୍ୟାଧୁନିକ ପ୍ରଯୁକ୍ତି ତଥା ବୈଷୟିକ ବିଦ୍ୟାରେ ସମୃଦ୍ଧ ଏହି ସ୍ୱନାମଧନ୍ୟ ସଂସ୍ଥାନ ବିଦ୍ୟାର୍ଥୀ/ବିଦ୍ୟାର୍ଥିନୀଙ୍କ ବୃତ୍ତିଗତ ଜୀବନ ଗଢ଼ିବା ଦିଗରେ ସମସ୍ତ ପ୍ରକାର ଶୈକ୍ଷିକ ସେବା ଉପଲବ୍ଧ କରାଇ ଆସୁଅଛି | இந்திரா ஐயர் / மாணவி VIT என்கிற பொறியியல் கல்லூரி கல்வியை வழங்குவது மட்டுமல்லாமல், மாணவர்களின் முகத்தில் தன்னம்பிக்கையும் பெருமிதமும் வழங்குகிற ஒரு கருவியாகும். எனது கல்லூரி விளையாட்டு மைதானம், ஒரு நூலகம் மற்றும் ஒரு அறிவியல் மண்டபம் போன்ற சிறந்த வசதிகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது. رفن کنیل / طالب علم ودیالانکر انسٹی ٹیوٹ آف ٹیکنالوجی، ٹکنالوجی پر منحصر تعلیم کے لئے درکار تمام جدید سہولیات سے آراستہ ہے۔ یہاں کے ماہر، تجربہ کار اور مشفق اساتذہ کی سرپرستی اور ان سے حاصل ہونے والی رہنمائی زندگی کے حقیقی اہداف کے حصول میں معاون ہے۔ Ameya & Aditi / A VIT Couple As they say, “College days are the BEST days of your life”, it was indeed so for Ameya and I. We started out as classmates, then friends, then best friends and now life partners. VIT gave us some of the best memories of our lives like participating in VERVE as a volunteer to actually successfully organizing it, from the intense vivas to long movie watching hours after the exams, from unknown faces on the first day of college to being lifelong friends and most of all, made us better individuals. I am glad I took the decision of joining VIT and wish all the prospective students the very best for their journey here. It will be Worth It! ਸਰਨਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਸਲੁਜਾ / ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀ VIT ਜਿਸ ਵਿਚ ਉਹ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸਹੂਲਤਾਂ ਹਨ ਜੋ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਰਬੋਤਮ ਬਣਨ ਵਿਚ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ || ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਰੋਤ ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਇੱਕ ਚੰਗੀ ਲਾਇਬ੍ਰੇਰੀ, e-learning ਸਮਰੱਥਾ, ਸਮਰਪਿਤ ਅਧਿਆਪਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਕਾਰਾਤਮਕ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ ਨਾਲ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਸਰਵਪੱਖੀ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ || ਮੈਨੂੰ ਅਜਿਹੇ ਨਾਮਵਰ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਬਣਨ ਤੇ ਮਾਣ ਹੈ || संकेत सभरवाल / भूतपूर्व विद्यार्थी VIT में नेतृत्व की टीम शैक्षिक दिशा में जैसे सैद्धांतिक व व्यवहारिक अभ्यास, अनुसन्धान तकनीकी ज्ञान, संस्कृति, पर्यावरण, स्वास्थ्य और खेल आदि क्षेत्रों के चहुमुखी विकास की ओर ध्यान केंद्रित करते है। वर्षों से यह मिश्रण सूर्य की किरणों की भांति विभिन्न उपलब्धियों और प्रशंसा के प्रकाश में प्रकाशित हो युवा छात्रों का मार्ग दर्शन करने में अग्रसर है। Shakti Nandan / Hiring Partner, Tata Consultancy Services VIT has been a long standing partner of TCS and together we have helped give direction to many careers. Vidyalankar as an institute of repute has been pivotal in preparing the students for a corporate role and these students over the years have played an invaluable role in the organization’s growth journey. The college has always encouraged and supported the academia-industry partnership by hosting several seminars, webinars, discussion forums and student connect sessions on subjects ranging from technology to soft skill development. The college’s journey from the past few years have been incredible in terms of the quality of the students and the exposure that is being provided to them. Kaustab & Sanjukta / A VIT Couple VIT is an educational institution which attracts and grooms students from different backgrounds. I met some very intelligent, talented and creative folks on campus which included my best friend and life partner Sanjukta. We were and still are very different in our personalities however we found that each of us could thrive at VIT and pursue whatever we wanted for our individual careers. The friendship that we had built at VIT through all the years of studies and extra curricular activities had stood the test of time when we did tie the knot many years later. I hear from our dear faculty and students that VIT is getting even more diverse and even more active in an all-round manner. Here’s wishing all the students and faculty the very best for the future! Nagesh Utekar / Director, Rescare Medisystem (I) Pvt. Ltd. VIT encourages students to be more practical and industry oriented . From organising industry guest lectures or organising Technical fest gives student the freedom to create Products for Future and interact with Industry to understand their needs right when they are learning. They have developed inhouse skill labs which imparts hands on training. The faculty are very keen and try to learn new things out of their interest so it could benefit the students. They organize visits to Hospitals,Industry, R&D and Design centers for students growth. Neelesh_Shinde / Chief Technical Officer, Jupiter Hospital As a passion towards Biomedical Engineering, I had conducted lectures on “Visionary role of Biomedical Engineer in healthcare industry” at Vidyalankar Institute of Technology. Since 2011 Jupiter Hospital is associated with VIT and we have facilitated Hospital visits, hands-on training, interactive sessions for students of Biomedical stream. Vidyalankar college is keen in giving on field practical exposure to biomedical engineers who will be the future innovators in the game of healthcare transformation in India.

text: About E-Cell The Entrepreneurship Cell (E -Cell) at Vidyalankar Institute of Technology (VIT) is a student -run organisation dedicated to nurturing a culture of entrepreneurship, innovation, and problem -solving on campus. Launched on 30 April 2026, E -Cell serves as the institute's dedicated launchpad for aspiring student founders — bridging the gap between a raw idea and a functioning startup. E-Cell provides students with access to mentorship from industry leaders, funding guidance, workshops, pitch competitions, and hands -on exposure to the startup ecosystem. Whether you are exploring your first business idea or actively building a venture, E-Cell equips you with the tools, community, and confidence to take the next step. Operating under the tagline "Ideas  Action  Impact", E-Cell believes that every student has the potential to create meaningful change — and it exists to make that journey a reality. Objectives ■ Foster an entrepreneurial mindset among students. ■ Support end-to-end idea-to-startup development. ■ Connect students with mentors, founders, and investors. ■ Promote innovation, collaboration, and problem-solving. ■ Create a sustainable startup ecosystem within the institute. ■ Encourage execution, accountability, and smart risk-taking. text: Japan Tech Immersion: Global Industry Experience Educultural Tour Japan is a global leader in science, technology, and innovation, known for its precision, sustainability, and seamless blend of tradition with progress. From bullet trains to robotics, and global giants like Toyota and Sony, Japan continues to shape the future. This transformative Edu-Cultural Tour was organized by Vidyalankar Institute of Technology, Mumbai, and coordinated by Prof. Sonaali Borkar, giving students firsthand exposure to Japan’s excellence and culture. Japan 3 to 10 June, 2025 Home of cherry blossoms and bullet trains. 1 ATTRACTIONS M a j o r v i s i t ed Sophia University Rinkai Disaster Management Park Miraikan Mt.Fuji Shibuya Crossing Hachiko Statue Sensoji Temple Total Participants Students Faculty Where every train is on time and every garden is in balance. NaraArashiyama Bamboo Forest Osaka Castle Dotonbori Tokyo Tower 2 Day 1 Arrival in Tokyo (04 June 2025) The journey began with the arrival at Haneda International Airport, Tokyo, marking the start of an immersive and enriching experience in Japan. The efficiency of immigration procedures, cleanliness of the surroundings, and the polite, organized conduct of airport staff offered an immediate glimpse into the country’s renowned discipline and hospitality. From the very first interaction, Japan’s commitment to order, precision, and respectful service set a tone of admiration and curiosity, paving the way for the days of learning and exploration that followed. Where tradition meets tomorrow — Welcome to Japan. Haneda Airport 3 Day 2 Academic & Scientific Exposure (05 June 2025) Sophia University, Tokyo The highlight of this visit was an engaging session with Prof. John Joseph Puthenkalam. He introduced the students to Japan’s innovative approaches to sustainability, climate resilience, and global academic collaborations. One of his students presented India as a case study, bridging the experience between two cultures sparking discussions. Precision, peace, and progress — the spirit of Japan.4 Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science & Innovation From humanoid robot to space missions, the Miraikan showcased Japan’s scientific foresight and public science engagement. Rinkai Disaster Management Park Realistic earthquake simulations and disaster preparedness systems highlighted Japan’s urban safety, community training, and resilience. In Japan, technology bows to culture. 5 Sensoji Shrine Tokyo TowerZojoji Temple Day 3 Tokyo City Tour (06 June 2025) Students explored the Tokyo Tower, Zojoji Temple, Asakusa Sensoji shrine— experiencing the unique contrast of futuristic skyscrapers and traditional architecture. The group appreciated the cleanliness, public transport systems, and overall discipline in the city’s daily rhythm. Clean streets, clear minds — the Japanese way. Meiji Shrine 6 Arakurayama Sengen Park Ashi Lake Day 4 Mt. Fuji (07 June 2025) A breathtaking blend of natural beauty and seamless travel as the group journeyed from Tokyo to Kyoto with scenic halts at Mt. Fuji and Lake Ashi. Mt. Fuji — where nature stands in perfect stillness. 7 Arashiyama Bamboo Forest Kyoto Tower Deer Park, Nara Day 5 Kyoto & Nara (08 June 2025) Day 5 was for Japan’s rich cultural and spiritual heritage exploration - the historically significant cities of Kyoto and Nara. The journey felt like stepping back in time, where every temple, pathway, and shrine reflected Japan’s deep- rooted values of peace, respect, and mindfulness.. Efficient transportation makes travel between these destinations seamless. From sacred foxes to street cats, Japan cherishes all life forms.8 Shin-Osaka Station Katsuoji Suica Card Osaka Castle Day 6 Osaka via Shinkansen (09 June 2025) Shinkansen, Japan’s renowned bullet train. This high-speed journey offered students a firsthand experience of Japan’s world-class transportation system—known for its remarkable punctuality, comfort, and cutting-edge engineering. Upon arrival in Osaka, students were encouraged to explore the city through self-managed group activities, allowing them to experience local life, cuisine, and culture independently. A nation of quiet strength and loud innovation. Journey in Shinkansen 9 Day 7 Departure from Kansai (10 June 2025) With hearts full and minds expanded, the contingent departed from Kansai International Airport, carrying memories of discipline, technological marvels, and cultural beauty that will last a lifetime. The airport’s smooth operations and polite service were a final reflection of Japan’s precision and grace. Respect. Discipline. Innovation. That’s Japan. Kansai International Airport (KIX) 10 Shibuya Crossing Hachiko Statue Fushimi Inari Ninenzaka, Kyoto Among Japan’s many iconic landmarks, a few stand out not just for their visual appeal but for the deep cultural stories they carry. Its ability to honor loyalty, embrace progress, and preserve spirituality, all in one breathtaking narrative. Learning from a land that never stops evolving. JAPAN’S GREATNESS 11 Japan's history is a rich tapestry woven from the eras of samurai warriors, feudal shogunates, and imperial rule. Historic towns and sites, from ancient wooden temples to well- preserved castles, provide a window into the country's storied past. These landmarks showcase the evolution of Japan's governance, culture, and architecture over centuries. Temples teach what textbooks can't — the rhythm of reverence. Fushimi Inari Katsuō-ji Kiyomizu-dera Sensō-ji Sinto Shrine Shitennoji 12 Sushi Macha Icecream A lady in Kimono Jizo Statues, Zojoji Authentic Ramen DarumaUdon Noodles A culture that bows in greeting and rises in innovation. title: SOUTH_KOREA_Tour_booklet.pdf
text: 2019 ED T UR INTERNATIONAL VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology Accredited A+ by NAAC SOUTH KOREA South Korea rd th 23 – 30 June, 2019 South Korea is the world's 11th largest economy and a global leader in the industrial and technological sectors that not only holds a strong presence in Asia but also in the rest of the world. Seoul is ranked as the world's "Leading Digital City" and a "Tech Capital of the World". South Korea is also among the world's most technologically advanced and digitally-connected countries; it has the third most broadband Internet users among the OECD countries and is a global leader in electronics and digital displays. VIT organised this Edutour where Students and Staff members experienced the hustle bustle of the city life with the serenity of nature nearby, where both technology and tradition co-exist. 1 MAJOR ATTRACTIONS 2 Gyeongbokgung Palace Samsung Innovation Museum SK T.um Samsung D'Light Seoul National University POSCO Steel Plant Hyundai Motors Factory & Hyundai Heavy Industry Everland Theme Park Total Participants Students 20 Faculty Members 04 Gyeongbokgung Palace th 24 June, Monday Gyeongbokgung was the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty. Built in 1395, it is located in northern Seoul, South Korea. The largest of the Five Grand Palaces built by the Joseon dynasty, Gyeongbokgung served as the home of Kings of the Joseon dynasty, the Kings' households, as well as the government of Joseon. Gyeongbokgung continued to serve as the main palace of the Joseon dynasty until the premises were destroyed by ﬁre during the Imjin War (1592–1598) and abandoned for two centuries. However, in the 19th century, all of the palace's 7,700 rooms were later restored under the leadership of Prince Regent Heungseon during the reign of King Gojong. Some 500 buildings were restored on a site of over 40 hectares. The architectural principles of ancient Korea were incorporated into the tradition and appearance of the Joseon royal court. 3 4 Samsung Innovation Museum Through innovations, from the discovery of electricity to the latest smartphones, the electronics industry has added new value to our lives. Samsung Innovation Museum exhibits the history and the future of such innovations brought by the electronics industry. That is also why it is named the Innovation Museum. It not only shows the history of the electronics industry but the contributions that Samsung Electronics has made in the IT industry with its leading semi- conductor, display and mobile technologies. The three halls at the museum are - Era of Inventors, Era of Corporate Innovation, and Era of Creation. th 25 June, Tuesday As the ﬁrst Korean mobile carrier that commercialized LTE and the ﬁrst in the world to commercialize LTE-A, SK Telecom led the world's telecommunication industry. They opened the ﬁrst-generation analogue mobile phone era and led the world in commercializing the CDMA and HSDPA technologies.. At “T.UM”, it showcases diverse technologies and services that are expected to be widely used in the upcoming 5G era. Their vision is to connect new value and the future world through passion and innovation. 5 SK T.um th 25 June, Tuesday 6 Samsung D'Light 'Samsung D'light' is a global exhibition space that showcases the latest product lineup by Samsung Electronics built to let you have fun with it's most innovative technologies. The name d'light combines the words 'digital' and 'light' to correlate with the company's vision of being 'a guiding light to the digital world' and sharing the excitement and delight of digital technology through interaction with visitors. The 'd' also carries with it the connotation of 'dynamic,' 'dream,' and 'diversity.' th 25 June, Tuesday Seoul National University honors the ideals of liberal education and aims to teach students a lifelong love of learning that will form the basis for continuous personal growth. The mission of Seoul National University in the twenty-ﬁrst century is to create a vibrant intellectual community where students and scholars join together in building the future. As Korea's leading research university, Seoul National University is committed to diversifying its student body and faculty, fostering global exchange, and promoting path-breaking research in all ﬁelds of knowledge. 7 Seoul National University th 26 June, Wednesday 8 POSCO Steel Plant POSCO (formerly Pohang Iron and Steel Company) is a South Korean steel-making company headquartered in Pohang, South Korea. It had an output of 42 million tonnes of crude steel in 2015, making it the world's fourth-largest steelmaker by this measure. In 2010, it was the world's largest steel manufacturing company by market value. POSCO takes great efforts to realize the values it deems important, such as putting substance ﬁrst, emphasizing execution, and pursuing beneﬁts. It's core values are 'Safety,' 'Win-Win,' 'Ethics' and 'Creativity.' th 27 June, Thursday Hyundai Motors Ulsan Plant is the world's largest single plant. It is made up of ﬁve independent factories, with approximately 32,000 personnel producing an average of 5,800 vehicles per day. Another surprising feature of this complex is the 600,000 trees planted within the area, making the plant a factory surrounded by a forest. Hyundai Heavy Industries Co., Ltd. (or HHI) is the world's largest shipbuilding company. Its headquarters are in Ulsan, South Korea. HHI was founded in 1972 by Chung Ju-yung as a division of the Hyundai Group, and in 1974, completed building its ﬁrst ﬂeet of ships. In 2002, the company was spun-off from its parent company. HHI has four core business divisions: Shipbuilding, Offshore & Engineering, Industrial Plant & Engineering, and Engine & Machinery. 9 Hyundai Motors Factory & Hyundai Heavy Industry th 28 June, Friday 10 Everland Theme Park Everland is South Korea's largest theme park. Located at the Everland Resort in Yongin, a city in Gyeonggi-do, it receives 7.3 million visitors annually[2] and was ranked sixteenth in the world for amusement park attendance in 2014. Along with its main attractions, Everland includes a zoo and water park known as Caribbean Bay. Everland is operated by Samsung C&T Corporation (formerly known as Samsung Everland, Cheil Industries), which is a subsidiary of the Samsung Group. This park was formerly called "Jayeon Nongwon" which roughly translates to "natural farm th 29 June, Saturday 11 EDUCATIONAL JOURNEYS and Expeditions ! Memories... 12 Key Takeaways World Class Automobile Industry Korean Heavy Industries Exposure to Future Technology & Projects Unique experiences Glimpses of Culture and History Iconic Monuments and landmarks Peer Bonding 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 13 STUDENTS Speak “ I have visited a few countries before but this was my ﬁrst international trip with my peers. My experience was amazing. We visited many industries which we probably would not visit with family. The trip was well organised and was a perfect balance between educational & recreational visits. The team & especially our teachers took good care of us. I got opportunity to make new friends & create unforgettable memories. The one week of my summer break spent in South Korea was deﬁnitely fruitful. It was the most valuable learning experience I have had & I am very grateful to my college for giving us this wonderful opportunity! - Aarya Tadvalkar, TE CMPN A “ The edutour to South Korea was indeed an enriching experience for me. We visited various industries, some places of cultural importance & some fun places too. It was a great exposure not only to the real world industries but also to travelling to a different country with a new language and different culture. I would like thank our institute for providing us this opportunity. We were accompanied by some faculty members who were very supportive and took good care of us. Overall it was a great experience. - Sai Shekhar Nimkar, TE CMPN A VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology Accredited A+ by NAAC

title: Singapore_Malaysia_tour_booklet.pdf
text: VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology Singapore Malaysia Edu Tour2011 Singapore Malaysia Singapore, an island city-state oﬀ southern Malaysia, is a global ﬁnancial center with a tropical climate and multicultural population. Singapore is a global hub for education, entertainment, ﬁnance, healthcare, human capital, innovation, logistics, manufacturing, technology, tourism, trade, and transport. The city ranks highly in numerous international rankings, and has been recognised as the most "technology-ready" nation (WEF), top International-meetings city (UIA), city with "best investment potential" (BERI), world's smartest city, world's safest country, world's most competitive economy, third least-corrupt country, third-largest foreign exchange market, third-largest ﬁnancial centre, third-largest oil reﬁning and trading centre, ﬁfth-most innovative country, and the second-busiest container port. The Economist has ranked Singapore as the most expensive city to live in, since 2013. It is identiﬁed as a tax haven. The nation is known for its transition from a developing to a developed country in a single generation under the leadership of its founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew. Major Attractions Genting City Tour Malaysia City Tour Singapore Sentosa Night Safari Multimedia University Malaysia Total Participants Students 14 Faculty members 02 Multimedia University Multimedia University is a private university in Malaysia. The university has campuses, located in Melaka, Cyberjaya and Iskandar Puteri. The university hosts 9 faculties and 19 research centres. The Faculty of Engineering (FOE) is based in Cyberjaya. It oﬀers bachelor's degrees accredited by the Washington Accord in Electrical, Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications, Nanotechnology, and Optical Engineering. The Faculty of Engineering and Technology (FET), based in Melaka, oﬀers courses in Electronics and Mechanical Engineering. The majors oﬀered by the FET Electronics Engineering courses are Robotics and Automation, and Telecommunications. City Tour, Singapore-Malaysia Malaysia is a Southeast Asian country occupying parts of the Malay Peninsula and the island of Borneo. It's known for its beaches, rainforests and mix of Malay, Chinese, Indian and European cultural inﬂuences. The capital, Kuala Lumpur, is home to colonial buildings, busy shopping districts such as Bukit Bintang and skyscrapers such as the iconic, 451m-tall Petronas Twin Towers. Singapore city tour surrounds with popular districts like Chinatown, Little India and Marina Bay. A great activity for the start of your trip, this half-day tour introduces you to top attractions like the Merlion, Colonial Landmarks like City Hall and cultural sites like Thian Hock Keng Temple. Orchid Perfumes, Artefacts and Miniatures, Coconut Jam, Tiger Balm products are some of the famous shopping items for tourists in Singapore. Sentosa Sentosa is an island resort oﬀ Singapore’s southern coast, connected to the city by road, cable car, pedestrian boardwalk and monorail. By Sentosa Station, Tiger Sky Tower has panoramic views that can stretch as far as Indonesia. On the south coast, Palawan Beach is lined with food stalls and bars, and has a suspension bridge to a small oﬀshore island. Palm-lined, crescent-shaped Tanjong Beach is more tranquil. MALAYSIA Genting Genting Singapore PLC is a Singapore-based regional leisure, hospitality and integrated resorts development specialist listed on the main board of the Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited. The principal activities of the company’s subsidiaries include developing and operating large scale integrated resorts, investments, casino operations, provision of information technology application related services as well as marketing support services to leisure and hospitality related businesses and investments. Botanic Gardens The Singapore Botanic Gardens is a 160-year-old tropical garden located at the fringe of Singapore's Orchard Road shopping district. It is one of three gardens, and the only tropical garden, to be honoured as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Botanic Gardens has been ranked Asia's top park attraction since 2013, by TripAdvisor Travellers' Choice Awards. It was declared the inaugural Garden of the Year, International Garden Tourism Awards in 2012, and received Michelin's three-star rating in 2008. We had a great time throughout the trip, be it University tour, city tour, or the theme park. I made many new friends on the tour. Our teachers were very caring, and they made sure that everything was at its best. I have the best memories with me, and I urge my junior friends to take up such educational visits in the future. Kewal Dedhia SE, ETRX C “ As a student, I have never missed educational visits in my life. I never thought that I will be going on an International Edu Tour but thanks to VIT for arranging one for us. Singapore and Malaysia are amazing countries and one should never miss a chance to visit them. I learnt so many new things during the tour like art and culture, technology, travel, adventure etc. We had a very good time during our visit and the memories which I have gathered will remain with me lifelong. I am looking forward for more such international Edu Tours. VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology

title: Germany_Tour_booklet.pdf
text: GermanY Edu Tour VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology 2017 Year 1 Why Edu Tours? International Expose students to new cultures Creates an interest in new professions Informal learning environment Expose students to cuisines, infrastructure and lifestyle Reinforce classroom material by exposing students to real-world situations Teaches professionalism Expose students to di�erent learning styles rd th 3 - 8 July, 2017 Germany Germany is a global leader in science and technology as its achievements in the ﬁelds of science and technology have been signiﬁcant. Research and development eﬀorts form an integral part of the economy. The Nobel Prize has been awarded to 108 German laureates. It produces the second highest number of graduates in science and engineering (31%) after South Korea. In the beginning of the 20th century, German laureates had more awards than those of any other nation, especially in the sciences (physics, chemistry, and physiology or medicine). 2 Major Attractions Stuttgart University Wilhelma Zoo Mercedes B enzM useum BMW factory Hohenzollern Castle Olympic Stadium Deutsches Museum Rhine River Cruise 34 06 Students Faculty Total Participants The University of Stuttgart is a research university located in Stuttgart, Germany. It was founded in 1829 and is organized into 10 faculties. It is one of the oldest technical universities in Germany with highly ranked programs in civil, mechanical, industrial and electrical engineering. The University of Stuttgart is one of the leading technically oriented universities in Germany with global signiﬁcance. It sees itself as a center of university-based, non- university, and industrial research. Furthermore, it takes a role as a guarantor of research-based teaching, focused on quality and holism. The Stuttgart Way means an interdisciplinary integration of engineering, natural sciences, humanities, and social sciences based on the fundamentals of cutting-edge research at a disciplinary level. Stuttgart University 4 rd 3 July, Monday rd 3 July, Monday Wilhelma Zoo Wilhelma is a zoological-botanical garden in Stuttgart in the Bad Cannstatt district in the north of the city on the grounds of a historic castle. Wilhelma Zoo is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Baden-Württemberg, seeing more than 2 million visitors annually. The Zoo and Botanical Garden have been staﬀed since 1846. The Moorish Revival style echoing the Alhambra have been maintained and supplemented since 1960. Today, the zoo has an area of about 30 hectares, houses around 11,500 animals from around the world composed of roughly 1,200 species and roughly 6000 plants from all climates. Of Germany's zoos, Wilhelma's collection ranks second to the Berlin Zoological Garden. 5 The Mercedes-Benz Museum is an automobile museum in Stuttgart, Germany. It covers the history of the Mercedes-Benz brand and the brands associated with it. Stuttgart is home to the Mercedes-Benz brand and the international headquarters of Daimler AG. The museum provides visitors with free audio tours in a variety of languages. In 2007, the museum was visited by 860,000 people. Visitors are also oﬀered the opportunity to take a tour of the nearby Untertürkheim engine factory. The factory produces many of the company's diesel engines. th 4 July, Tuesday Mercedes Benz Museum 6 th 4 July, Tuesday Hohenzollern Castle Hohenzollern Castle is the ancestral seat of the imperial House of Hohenzollern. The third of three hilltop castles built on the site, it is located atop Mount Hohenzollern, above and south of Hechingen, on the edge of the Swabian Jura of central Baden-Württemberg, Germany. With over 350,000 visitors per year Hohenzollern castle is one of the most visited castles in Germany. 7 BMW is a German multinational company which produces automobiles and motorcycles. The company was founded in 1916 as a manufacturer of aircraft engines, which it produced from 1917 until 1918 and again from 1933 to 1945. Automobiles are marketed under the brands BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce, and motorcycles are marketed under the brand BMW Motorrad. In 2015, BMW was the world's twelfth largest producer of motor vehicles, with 2,279,503 vehicles produced. BMW is headquartered in Munich and produces motor vehicles in Germany, Brazil, China, India, South Africa, the United Kingdom, and the United States. BMW Factory 8 th 5 July, Wednesday Olympiastadion Olympiastadion is a sports stadium at Olympiapark Berlin in Berlin, Germany. It was originally built by Werner March for the 1936 Summer Olympics. During the Olympics, the record attendance was thought to be over 100,000. Today the stadium is part of the Olympiapark Berlin. Since renovations in 2004, the Olympiastadion has a permanent capacity of 74,475 seats and is the largest stadium in Germany for international football matches. Olympiastadion is a UEFA category four stadium and one of the world's most prestigious venues for sporting and entertainment events. Besides its use as an athletics stadium, the arena has built a footballing tradition. Since 1963, it has been the home of the Hertha BSC . It hosted three matches in the 1974 FIFA World Cup. It was renovated for the 2006 FIFA World Cup, when it hosted six matches, including the ﬁnal. 9 th 5 July, Wednesday The Deutsches Museum in Munich, Germany, is the world's largest museum of science and technology, with about 28,000 exhibited objects from 50 ﬁelds of science and technology. It receives about 1.5 million visitors per year. The museum was founded on 28 June 1903, at a meeting of the Association of German Engineers as an initiative of Oskar von Miller. It is the largest museum in Munich. For a period of time the museum was used to host pop and rock concerts including The Who, Jimi Hendrix and Elton John. th 6 July, Thursday Deutsches Museum 10 Rhine River Cruise The Rhine is one of the major European rivers, which has its sources in Switzerland and ﬂows in a mostly northerly direction through Germany and the Netherlands, emptying into the North Sea. One can sit in a boat and enjoy cruising along the waterfalls at Rhine. 11 Endless Learnings ! 12 01 02 03 04 05 06 World Class Automobile Industry Exposure to Future Technology and Projects Unique experiences Glimpses of Culture and History Iconic Monuments and landmarks Peer Bonding Key Takeaways 13 They say “Germans respect you if you respect time.” Germans are very punctual in whatever they do, which made me realise the importance of time during this Edu tour. German technology, industries and their architectures are simply fantastic. Visiting the museums and industries of luxury vehicles producers Mercedes Benz and BMW made me believe in creativity, uniqueness and the ability to expand in technology. We enjoyed western cuisine every day for lunch and Indian food for dinner. This trip was highly beneﬁcial as it made all of us independent and curious enough to learn about more cultures and technological advancements happening in time. I will be overwhelmed to guide my juniors to join such educational trips which are organised by VIT. - Varshini Sundaresan, S.E EXTC - A I was visiting Germany for the ﬁrst time and so I was excited as well as a bit anxious since I was travelling to a foreign country for the ﬁrst time without my parents. But the faculty of VIT and tour manager who accompanied us managed everything in a systematic manner. The itinerary was meticulously planned which gave us enough time for the educational visits and leisure events. Going to Germany for an Edu Tour was a correct decision because I got to visit the BMW and Mercedes Benz plants which is not possible if someone visits Germany for a regular tour. Most of the Engineering colleges do not arrange international educational tours which limits the amount of exposure the students receive throughout the B.E. program. VIT did a great job by organizing this Edu Tour because it helped the students to gain knowledge and a diﬀerent experience which they would cherish for life! - Neil Dani, S.E ETRX - C 14 VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology VIT Vidyalankar Institute of Technology

Admission • Admission will be done on the basis of inter-se-merit of the candidates who have applied to the institute level rounds within the due date and on the basis of the rules published in the ‘Information Brochure’ by the Competent Authority, Maharashtra State, for admissions to Undergraduate Engineering Courses. • The candidate shall report to the Institute on the date and time mentioned in the Schedule with requisite amount of fee and required ORIGINAL documents. Candidate shall produce ALL the applicable original documents at the time of document verification during the counselling round. In case a candidate has taken admission elsewhere he/she will be required to submit original retention certificate of that Institute and submit all the original documents within two days. • The seat will be allotted to the candidate based on her/his seat availability, Inter- se – merit, category, choice of seat type i.e. IQ/ACAP and branch preferred. • If a candidate of higher merit reports late during the process of counselling, the candidate shall be considered for allotment of a seat available at that point. The decision of the Authorities of Institute shall be final and binding. • If the candidate accepts the offered seat s/he shall confirm her/his admission immediately by payment of requisite fees and submission of ORIGINAL DOCUMENTS with self-attested copies (2 each) and 2 passport size photographs to the admission cell. If the original documents are submitted to any other Institute the candidate is required to produce the retention certificate in ORIGINAL of that Institute and must submit the original documents within two days. • If candidate fails to pay FULL FEES AS APPLICABLE at the time of admission, the allotted seat shall be denied and the seat shall be allotted to the next eligible candidate. • On verification of all original documents and receipt of requisite fees, admission shall be confirmed on State CET Cell portal and Admission Team authorities shall issue an acknowledgement receipt to the candidate. 9. Cancellation of Admission Candidate can cancel admission on CET cell portal as per rules prescribed by the State CET Cell. Students are expected to visit admission cancellation desk at the Institute for completion of further formalities and collection of original documents. Refund if applicable shall be issued in due process. Principal

title: FE-NOTICE-FOR-WEBSITE-2026-27.pdf
text: First Year Engineering Academic Year 2026-27 1 07 September 2026 NOTICE All First Year Engineering students should note the following: First Year Engineering sessions (AY 2026-27) will commence on Tuesday, 08 September 2026. All newly admitted students are requested to report to the Institute and attend the sessions which will commence at 9:00 AM. The schedule and classrooms will be shared on the Notice Board outside First Year Engineering Office D103. 14 September to 18 September 2026 shall be non-instructional on account of Ganpati Festival. Orientation Program “Urja – The Spark Within” is organized for all First Year Engineering students on 21 and 22 September 2026. Students along with Parents are cordially invited to the Orientation Program. The Venue will be the Auditorium and the schedule for the same is as follows: Branch & Division Day & Date Timings Information Technology Divisions A, B, C Monday, 21 September 11:00 AM – 01:00 PM Computer Engineering Divisions A, B, C Monday, 21 September 02:00 PM – 04:00 PM Electronics & Computer Science Divisions A, B, C Tuesday, 22 September 11:00 AM – 01:00 PM Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering Divisions A, B Biomedical Engineering Division A Tuesday, 22 September 02:00 PM – 04:00 PM Please note that the National Anthem is played at 11:00 AM and National Song is played at 5:00 PM on the campus every day. All are required to stand in attentive position and display due respect. In case of any queries, you may contact: Prof. Sonaali Borkar (In-Charge, First Year Engineering) in D103 Prof. Meenakshi Nandula (Department Academic Officer) in D103 First Year Department Executives (Monday to Saturday between 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM) Mr. Harshad Lad: 8087111487 Mr. Prathamesh Gurav: 8451822309 Sd/- Principal Vidyalankar Institute of Technology First Year Engineering Academic Year 2026-27 2 Welcome Message from the Desk of First Year Engineering In-Charge My Dear First Year Engineering Students, A very warm welcome to a new semester and an exciting chapter in your engineering journey! As we begin, remember that our Student First approach remains at the heart of everything we do. Your growth, success and well-being are very important to us, and we are always here to support you. As you move forward, focus on three things: Toolset, Skillset and Mindset. Use the right tools to explore the fascinating world of engineering , keep sharpening your skills, and approach every challenge with a positive mindset, curiosity, confidence and a willingness to learn. This semester don’t just attend - participate. Don’t just learn - apply. Don’t wait for opportunities - step up and create them . Challenge yourself, try something new, make mistakes, learn, and keep moving forward. Believe in yourself, give it your best, and make every opportunity count. Take charge of your future. Keep growing to your full potential . May the start of your engineering journey be one of your best memories! Wishing you all an energetic, fulfilling and successful semester ahead! Warm regards, Sonaali Borkar In-Charge, First Year Engineering Vidyalankar Institute of Technology

text: Vidyalankar Institute of Technology Wadala (E), Mumbai 400 037 (Autonomous Institute affiliated to University of Mumbai) Guidelines for the Candidates reporting to Institute for admission Candidates shall report to the Institute to secure her/his admission as per the schedule published by the State CET Cell, Maharashtra. The process followed for CAP admissions shall be as given below: 1 Organize all the required documents, passport size-colored photographs and demand draft of applicable fees (if you are paying fees using demand draft) before you report to the Institute. 2 Keep Scrutiny Centre verification acknowledgement, Allotment acknowledgement and demand draft (if any) ready with you to display when you reach the Institute for reporting. 3 On visiting the Institute Proceed to the Computer Center, Block G. 4 Fill up ERP Applicant Data form and collect a copy of the form from the Computer Center with the help of Admission Officers available over there. 5 Proceed to lobby area outside the Admission Cell (M101). 6 Get your original documents, Self-attested photocopies, passport size photographs preverified and prepare the sets as advised by the Admission Officers on Document Pre-verification Desk outside M101. 7 Enter the Admission Cell (M101) only when instructed along with all the sets prepared. 8 Proceed to Document Verification Desk inside M101. 9 Get your original documents verified, confirm your admission in ERP and collect retention certificate from the Admission Officers over there. 10 Keep the retention certificate and demand draft (if any) ready with you. 11 Proceed to Account Desk and after payment collect your fees payment receipt. 12 Proceed to Admission Confirmation (on CET portal) Desk inside M101. 13 Get your admission confirmed on CET portal, submit all the sets of documents (including originals) and collect admission confirmation acknowledgement from the Admission Officer over there. 14 Proceed to Scholarship/Freeship Desk (applicable only for reserved category students) and submit the required documents. 15 Proceed to I-card desk, submit passport size-colored photographs (2 copies) and collect your temporary I-card from the Admission Officer over there. 16 Your Admission process is completed, and you can leave Admission Cell (M101) 17 Make sure that you have the following documents with you while leaving the Admission Cell: 1. Document Retention certificate 2. Fees payment receipt 3. State CET Cell confirmation acknowledgement 4. Temporary I-card Principal 1 Aug. 2026 Centralized Admission Process (CAP) Admissions (2026-27) Direct Second Year Engineering (B.Tech.)

The institute aims at providing organizations with talent who are an appropriate fit for the corporate world’s needs. The Training and Placement Cell, led by a senior and experienced person, has a focused approach on preparing students for recruitment. The institute maintains strong ties with the industry and arranges opportunities for student interactions through industrial visits, guest lectures, internships, conferences and workshops to help them to get a corporate perspective. PLACEMENT oUTCOME @VIT Placement @ VIT Placement Details of Batch 2026 GLIMPSES Campus Placements by Indian Navy Campus Placements by TCS Campus Placements by Works Applications GLIMPSES The Campus Connect Program The Campus Connect Program An industry-academia partnership initiative Facilitates the alignment of engineering student’s skills with the industry requirements to create industry-ready professionals. The Career Counselling Cell at VIT Guides students on the career opportunities available, skills, practical training and languages useful to enhance employability. Dale Carnegie Training Program Is imparted to all students in two well defined modules-'Generation Next' in the First Year and 'Step Upto Professional Excellence' in the Third Year with emphasis on basic communication etiquette and pre-recruitment training. Subject Specific Aptitude Tests Aptitude and subject specific tests for 3rd year students, gives them feedback on their performance and areas of improvement. COMPREHENSIVE PREPLACEMENT TRAINING Focus on imparting technological abilities for application at the work place, personality development, enhancing communication skills, and extensive exercises to inculcate analytical and verbal abilities to empower job aspirants. The students are trained on aspects like: Higher Studies Counselling Resume Writing GATE Preparation & Career Opportunities Alumni Success Stories International University Guidance Competitive Exam Guidance The motive behind these training sessions is to improve: Self Esteem Communication Abilities Motivational Skills Technical Skills Workplace Behavior CV and Interview skills PLACEMENT OFFICER Dr. Prashant Lokhande Email Id: prashant.lokhande@vit.edu.in Office Location: M102 Office Timings: 9.00am to 6.00pm FAQ’S WHAT IS CAMPUS PLACEMENT? Companies which would like to recruit freshers visit the institutes, conduct the process of recruitment and recruit the students when they are in final year of engineering. It will be a day-long process. WHEN DO CAMPUS PLACEMENTS HAPPEN IN THE INSTITUTE? Normally, the campus placement procedure takes place in the middle of the seventh semester. It starts in the month of September and goes on till the end of the academic year and sometimes even beyond that. CAN EVERY STUDENT IN THE INSTITUTE PARTICIPATE IN CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Only those students who meet the eligibilty criteria given by the companies can participate. WHAT IS TO BE DONE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Students interested in the campus placements should register themselves with the placement cell when the notice is put up on Vidyalankarlive for the same. WHAT ARE THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA TO PARTICIPATE IN THE CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Various companies have different eligibility criteria. However, there are companies which do not have any eligibility criteria. All the students studying in the final year will become eligible in that case. Some of the eligibility criteria to participate in the campus placements are given below: SSC – 60% HSC – 60% Diploma – 60% Engineering aggregate marks – 60% Can/cannot have live KTs Can/cannot have Dead KTs Can/cannot have Gap during Engineering/Gap during education Companies will have all the above or some as the eligibility criteria. WHAT ARE THE STAGES OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS? The following are the stages of recruitment: Pre-placement Talk Aptitude Test/Technical Test (Online/Pen and Paper) Group Discussion. Technical/HR Interview. MR (Management Round) Interview. WHAT IS APTITUDE TEST? Consists of verbal reasoning, logical reasoning and mathematics. Duration of the test varies, depending on the company. Every company has minimum marks section-wise or overall. Some companies have negative marking also Those who clear the aptitude test will go to the next round of the selection process. WHAT IS GROUP DISCUSSION? Group discussion is conducted to evaluate the students on the basis of knowledge on current affairs, communication, leadership qualities and group behavior. Those who clear the group discussion will go to the next round of the selection process. WHAT IS PERSONAL INTERVIEW (HR)? HR interviews are conducted to evaluate soft skills and confidence. It ensures that the company is not only hiring a person who is good technically but also someone who fits in to the company and its culture. The attitude of the students is tested in this round of interview. When a student is giving personal interview, how he/she enters and walks in to the room, how he/she sits, how and what he/she answers are all important. WHAT IS TECHNICAL INTERVIEW? Conducted to test the technical knowledge of the students. Questions will be asked on the basics of engineering subjects studied. In case a student has done any certification course, his knowledge in that area is also tested. WILL THE RESULTS BE DECLARED ON THE SAME DAY OF THE CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Yes. It will be declared on the same day by many companies. But a few companies will mail the results later. WHAT ARE THE DOCUMENTS TO BE CARRIED BY THE THE STUDENTS ON THE DAY OF CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? College identity card. Updated resume in the given format (3 copies) Original and photocopies of mark sheets and other certification if any. 2 passport size photographs. Students should be formally dressed and follow code of conduct. IS FORMAL DRESS COMPULSORY? WHAT ARE THE THINGS TO BE DONE ON THE DAY BEFORE THE CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Yes. Every student should be attired in formal wear. Please go thorough the code of conduct. WILL THERE BE ANY KIND OF PRE-PLACEMENT TRAINING ORGANIZED BY THE INSTITUTE FOR THE STUDENTS GOING FOR CAMPUS PLACEMENTS? Yes. Pre-placement training will start from the fourth semester onwards and it will continue till the campus placements begin. WHICH ARE THE COMPANIES THAT VISIT OUR CAMPUS? Please go through the list of the companies mentioned under placements on website. CAN ONE STUDENT GET MORE THAN ONE OFFER? No. Once a student is selected by any company, he will be out of the campus placement activities. However, if a company, which pays a salary difference of about 2 lakhs and above per annum, vists VIT all the students already selected will also be allowed. TIPS PRIOR TO THE CAMPUS PLACEMENTS Prepare well for the campus placements and avoid being overconfident and complacent. Give utmost importance to punctuality; reach the venue 30 minutes before the scheduled time. Be well-groomed and professionally dressed in formal wear during the entire process of the campus placements. Display your identity card throughout the placement process. Visit the websites of the recruiting companies to be well-aware of the recruiting companies. This will help you during HR interviews as there will be questions on this. Remember that you are an ambassador for your Institute and you are expected to project a positive image of your Institute. CHECKLIST Three passport size color photographs Photocopies and original certificates of SSC, HSC/Diploma and Engineering. For any reason, if mark sheet of any semester has not been issued by the University, the provisional mark sheet should be obtained from the college authorities. If the originals of SSC, HSC and DIPLOMA are with the college authorities, photocopies of the same should be carried. Three sets of your résumé. It should look impressive and be properly formatted and updated. DURING THE PRE-PLACEMENT TALK Switch off your mobile phones. Sign on the attendance sheet that will be circulated on the day of campus placements at our Institute and also at other institutes during pool campus. Be serious and attentive during the pre-placement talk. Maintain silence during the pre-placement talk and do not engage in side-talk with fellow candidates. Make a note of important points mentioned. There will be questions during the HR interviews on what has been told during the pre-placement talk. If the company speakers encourage you to ask questions at the end of the talk, communicate in a responsible and intelligent manner. Clarify doubts (if any) only at the end of pre-placement talk and do not interrupt the speakers during the pre-placement talk. Do not approach the company HR personnel directly. Always approach the college placement officer for any reason before and after the campus placements. DURING THE APTITUDE AND TECHNICAL TESTS Switch off your mobile phones. Be seated in the classrooms quietly till the team comes to conduct the aptitude test or technical test. Strictly avoid malpractices (like copying, discussing) during the tests. Do not get into any arguments for any reason with the supervisor/company representative present in the classroom. Carefully listen to and comply with all instructions given by the person conducting the test. Be present at the stipulated time of declaration of results of the aptitude test, group discussion and the final selection. AFTER CONCLUSION OF PLACEMENT ACTIVITIES Immediately after coming out of the interview room, write down the questions you were asked on the perforated sheet of the student diary and submit the same in the placement cell. This will help create a question bank for guiding your juniors. Once selected by a company, you will be ineligible for appearing for further placement.

title: Dr.MR-Tadvalkar-Memorial-Schlorship_2026-4.pdf
text: Dr. Madhukar R. Tadvalkar Memorial Scholarship - 2026 is awarded to Harsh Kudtarkar (24104A0023) Electronics & Tele Communication Engineering Dr. Deepak Phatak, Professor Emeritus, IIT-Bombay awarding Dr. Madhukar R. Tadvalkar Memorial Scholarship – 2026 to Harsh Kudtarkar with Shri Milind & Dr. Nayana Tadvalkar. He works relentlessly on technical tasks and demonstrates far more than just academic ability . He works with dedication, discipline, curiosity, and has true engineering mindset. He willingly invests long hours in understanding, designing, troubleshooting, learning new technologies, and improving his practical skills without losing enthusiasm. He persistently handles assignments, projects, coding, designing, testing, and innovation, setting him apart as future-ready professional. He also inspires peers through his sincerity and commitment to problem-solving attitude, proving that consistent hard work and passion are the strongest foundations for success in engineering and technology. Dr. Madhukar R. Tadvalkar(1935-2025) Born (8th January 1935) in a very simple Brahmin family at Akkalkot, Dist. Solapur, Dr . Madhukar R. Tadvalkar completed his school education studying in prestigious Haribhai Deokaran School, Solapur, staying at his uncle’s home. Considering family needs, he left education and joined Indian Railways at Ratlam, Rajasthan. Two years later, he joined as clerk at Mantralaya, Mumbai. He grew in his profession on merit with honesty, sincerity and dedication. His work was highly recognized and appreciated throughout his career. While serving, he continued his study of Marathi and Sanskrit literature, particularly the scriptures. His passion for literary studies and teaching became a side hustle for him as he began teaching students who were weak in the languages. Later in his career Maharashtra Government deputed him to Lal Bahadur Shastri Academy, Mussoorie, to teach Marathi language to IAS new recruits placed in Maharashtra state. His passion for study took him back to formal education and at the age of 42, began his Bachelor’s in Marathi language at G N Khalasa College at Matunga, Mumbai. He graduated from the University of Mumbai in 1986 with First Class. He continued his studies and completed M.A. in Marathi Literature in 1988 with First Class and First rank from University of Mumbai when he was honoured with N. C. Kelkar gold medal. During this period, he used to attend his office and study at the University Library, Churchgate in the evening. He was a truly passionate learner and studied completely for self- satisfaction & self- enrichment, meanwhile infusing a culture of learning and education in the family. He continued his pursuit for learning and earned his Ph.D. in Marathi Literature in 1997 at the age of 62. After retirement he took to deep studies of scriptures like Dyaneshwari, Dasbodh and Shrimad Bhagwad Geeta. In 2017 he wrote a commentary on selected verses of Shrimad Bhagwad Geeta, titled 'श्रीमद् भगवद्गीता: एक आस्वादक वाचन'. As a simple, humble and peaceful person, he left behind his beautiful handwriting as ornament and a collection of books as treasure! डॉ. मधुकर रा. तडवळकर (१९३५-२०२५) सोलापूर जिल्ह्यातील अक्कलकोट येथील एका अततशय साध्या ब्राह्मण क ु टुुंबात िन्मलेले डॉ. मधुकर आर. तडवळकर याुंनी त्ाुंचे शालेय जशक्षण सोलापूर येथील प्रतततित हररभाई देवकरण शाळेत त्ाुंच्या मामाांच्या घरी राहून पूणण क े ले. क ु टुुंबाच्या गरिा लक्षात घेऊन त्ाुंनी जशक्षण सोडले आजण रािस्थानातील रतलाम येथे भारतीय रेल्वेत रुिू झाले. दोन वर्ाांनुंतर, ते मु ुं बईतील म ुं त्रालयात जलतपक म्हणून रुिू झाले. त्ाुंनी प्रामाजणकपणा आजण समपणणाने गुणवत्तेवर आपला कार्यभाग वाढवला. त्ाुंच्या स ुं पूणण कारतकदीत त्ाुंच्या कायाणची खूप प्रश ुं सा आजण कौतुक झाले. सेवा करत असताना , त्ाुंनी मराठी आजण स ुं स्क ृ त सातहत्ाचा, तवशेर्तः स ुं स्क ृ त सातहत्ाचा अभ्यास सुरू ठेवला. सातहत्यत्क अभ्यास आजण अध्यापनाची त्ाुंची आवड त्ाुंच्यासाठी एक भाग बनली कारण त्ाुंनी भार्ाुंमध्ये कमक ु वत असलेल्या तवद्यार्थ्ाांना जशकवण्यास सुरुवात क े ली. त्ाुंच्या कारतकदीच्या उत्त र ाधाणत महार ाष्ट्र सर कार ने त् ाुंना महार ाष्ट्र र ाज्य ात तनयुक्त झालेल्या नवीन आयएएस अजधकाऱयाुंना लाल बहादूर शास्त्री अकादमी, मसुरी र्ेथे मराठी भार्ा जशकवण्यासाठी तनवडले. अभ्यासाची आवड त्ाुंना पुन्हा औपचाररक जशक्षणाकडे घेऊन गेली आजण वयाच्या ४२ व्या वर्ी त्ाुंनी मु ुं बईतील माटुुंगा येथील िी.एन. खालसा ववद्यालर्ात प्रवेश घेऊन १९८६ मध्ये मु ां बई ववद्यापीठाची पदवी प्रथम श्रेणीत प्राप्त क े ली. त्ाुंनी आपला अभ्यास सुरू ठेवला आजण १९८८ मध्ये मु ुं बई तवद्यापीठातून प्रथम श्रेणीत आजण प्रथम क्रमाुंकाने मराठी सातहत्ात एम.ए. पूणण क े ले. त्ावेळी त्ाुंना प्रा. एन.सी. क े ळकर सुवणणपदकाने सन्मातनत करण्यात आले. या काळात , ते त्ाुंच्या कायाणलयात िात असत आजण स ुं ध्याकाळी चचणगेट येथील तवद्यापीठ ग्र ुं थालयात अभ्यास करत असत. ते खरोखरच एक उत्साही तवद्याथी होते आजण त्ाुंनी आत्म-समाधान आजण आत्म - समृद्धीसाठी पूणणपणे अभ्यास क े ला , त्ाच वेळी क ु टुुंबात जशक्षण आजण जशक्षणाची स ुं स्क ृ ती तनमाणण क े ली. त्ाुंनी जशक्षणाचा पाठपुरावा सुरू ठेवला आजण १९९७ मध्ये वयाच्या ६२ व्या वर्ी त्ाुंनी मराठी सातहत्ात पीएच.डी. जमळवली. तनवृत्तीनुंतर त्ाुंनी ज्ञानेश्वरी, दासबोध आजण श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता यासारख्या धमणग्र ुं थाुंचा सखोल अभ्यास के ला. २०१७ मध्ये त् ाुंनी श्रीमद् भगवद्गीत ेत ील तनवडक श्लोकाुंवर 'श्रीमद् भगवद्गीत ा: एक आस्वादक वाचन' या शीर्णकाने एक पुस्तक ललहून प्रकालशत क े ले. एक साधी, नम्र आजण शाुंत व्यक्ती म्हणून, त्ाुंनी त्ाुंचे सु ुं दर हस्ताक्षर अल ुं कार म्हणून आजण पुस्तकाुंचा स ुं ग्रह खजिना म्हणून मागे सोडला! Dr. Madhukar R. Tadvalkar Memorial Scholarship Ms. Aarya Tadvalkar, alumna (BE Computer Engg, 2017 -2021) of Vidyalankar Institute of Technology, in memory of her grandfather, proposes Dr. Madhukar R. Tadvalkar Memorial Scholarship to studious, needy and deserving student at the Institute. This scholarship shall be instituted from the year 2026. The scholarship shall be in the form of amount of Rs. 50,000/-. Desirous students shall self -nominate, or teachers can recommend students for scholarship in the prescribed form. Ms. Aarya Tadvalkar, Dr. Nayana Tadvalkar, Shri Milind Tadvalkar Campus Director (VDT) & Ms Rashmi Deshpande Chairperson (VDT) shall select student for scholarship. Desirous students shall apply in proforma given below. Applicants may give additional information which may help in selection.
